artists.biography:
The Black Crowes are an American rock band formed in 1989. Their discography includes nine studio albums, four live albums and several charting singles. The band was signed to Def American Recordings in 1989 by producer George Drakoulias and released their debut album, Shake Your Money Maker, the following year. The follow-up, The Southern Harmony and Musical Companion, reached the top of the Billboard 200 in 1992.

After a hiatus between 2002 and 2005, the band released Warpaint, which hit number 5 on the Billboard chart. After the release of a double album, the greatest hits-like and mostly acoustic Croweology in August 2010, the band started a 20th anniversary tour that was followed by an ongoing second hiatus.

The band has opened for various rock acts such as Heart, Robert Plant, Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers, the Dave Matthews Band, the Grateful Dead, Aerosmith and ZZ Top, and performed live with Jimmy Page and Oasis, among others. The band has sold over 30 million albums, and is listed at number 92 on VH1's "100 Greatest Artists of Hard Rock". They were also labeled by Melody Maker as "The Most Rock 'n' Roll Rock 'n' Roll Band in the World" and the readers of Rolling Stone voted them 'Best New American Band' in 1990.

perplexity.description:
Three Snakes and One Charm, released on July 23, 1996, is the fourth studio album by American rock band The Black Crowes, issued through American Recordings and Angelus Entertainment. Musically, the album marks a return to the band's Southern rock roots, emphasizing a blend of blues-infused rock and soulful melodies that had characterized their earlier work. This stylistic shift followed the more experimental and dense sound of their previous album, Amorica (1994), re-centering their sound on classic rock and roots influences.

Within The Black Crowes' discography, Three Snakes and One Charm stands as a mature consolidation of their signature style, featuring 12 tracks that showcase the songwriting partnership of brothers Chris and Rich Robinson. The album includes standout songs such as "Under a Mountain," "Good Friday," and "Nebekanezer," which highlight the band’s ability to balance gritty rock energy with melodic depth. Commercially, the album reached No. 15 on the US Billboard 200, reflecting solid success though not matching the higher peaks of their earlier releases. Critically, it was well received for its cohesive sound and reaffirmation of the band’s Southern rock identity during a period of internal tensions and lineup changes.
